title: QUIC Connection Migration Hosted Proof Lane Verification
verification_method: Requirement-home tests, helper dry-run planning, workflow review, artifact inspection, and hosted workflow dispatch when external evidence is required.
preconditions: The external `quic-interop-runner` checkout includes `ngtcp2`, `picoquic`, `lsquic`, `quic-go`, `msquic`, and `neqo` peer slots.
Hosted dispatch has Docker Engine 28.1 or later, Python 3.12, and Wireshark packet-analysis tools available.
The repo-local helper remains responsible for image replacement, runner invocation, inventory output, and per-cell artifact capture.
scope: Verify that the repository exposes manual advisory hosted proof lanes for server-role connectionmigration against neqo, plus a blocked comparison lane for picoquic, lsquic, quic-go, msquic, and neqo, without promoting blocked cells or changing ordinary CI gates.
procedure: Review `.github/workflows/interop-runner-handshake.yml` and confirm the `connectionmigration-server-proof` and `connectionmigration-server-proof-blocked` profiles are `workflow_dispatch` only.
Confirm the green profile includes a server-role matrix cell against `neqo` for `connectionmigration`.
Confirm the blocked profile includes server-role matrix cells against `picoquic`, `lsquic`, `quic-go`, `msquic`, and `neqo` for `connectionmigration`.
Confirm every matrix cell invokes `scripts/interop/Invoke-QuicInteropRunner.ps1` with matrix-provided role, local implementation slot, peer slot, testcase, timeout, and artifact root.
Confirm each cell uploads a distinct artifact bundle with `if: always()`.
Run the focused requirement-home tests for `REQ-QUIC-INT-0018` and `REQ-QUIC-INT-0022`.
Run representative helper dry-run plans for server-role neqo, picoquic, lsquic, quic-go, and msquic connectionmigration cells.

When external evidence is required, dispatch `gh workflow run interop-runner-handshake.yml --repo incursa/quic-dotnet --ref main -f coverage_profile=connectionmigration-server-proof` and `gh workflow run interop-runner-handshake.yml --repo incursa/quic-dotnet --ref main -f coverage_profile=connectionmigration-server-proof-blocked` and inspect each uploaded `runner-report.json` plus selected output logs.
expected_result: The repository configuration provides opt-in hosted proof lanes that can collect per-cell artifacts for Incursa.Quic as the server role against neqo for the green connectionmigration cell, while keeping a blocked comparison lane for picoquic, lsquic, quic-go, msquic, and neqo, and keeping the major-peer-matrix profile and HTTP/3 out of scope.
status_summary: Planned for hosted execution. The repository now has split connectionmigration proof lanes and the helper inventory already classifies connectionmigration as supported/executed. The latest local migration proof still shows the quic-go cell failing and the earlier picoquic/lsquic attempt was blocked by image-signature validation, which is why the green lane now uses neqo while the blocked comparison lane keeps picoquic, lsquic, quic-go, msquic, and neqo visible. Full SpecTrace core validation remains blocked by the current baseline and is not claimed as passing by this artifact.

supplemental_sections.heading: Deferred Coverage
supplemental_sections.content: `http3` remains out of scope. `v2`, `rebind-port`, and `rebind-addr` remain prerequisite-blocked under the non-HTTP/3 inventory. `connectionmigration` now has a green hosted proof lane against `neqo` plus a blocked comparison lane against `picoquic`, `lsquic`, `quic-go`, `msquic`, and `neqo`, but the green lane itself still needs live corroboration before any support claim changes.
